cube.title: Cube by Before Semicolon
cube.intro: A headless, themeable web-component library for visual editors. Components are organized into action, form, layout, navigation, overlay, feedback, data display, media, charts, styling, editor, collaboration, icons, and theme categories.
cube.guideBody: Import Cube or a category to register its components immediately. Classes and headless bases are normal named exports. Module entrypoints use the installed WebComponent runtime; browser scripts use BFS. No initialization call or ready promise is required. Component entrypoints require a DOM.
cube.runtime: Browser scripts require the web-component runtime first. Charts also need the ECharts runtime, or a custom configureChartEngine loader. Media-only scripts do not load ECharts. The current npm release has not been replaced by this branch.
cube.themeBody: ThemeProvider accepts a site-builder ThemeDefinitionV1 document through theme or src. appearance accepts light, dark or system. CSS token names match site-builder; nested providers create explicit scopes. JSON theme files and CSS are generated into dist/themes.
cube.actionsBody: Buttons, grouped actions, selection controls, navigation, menus, toolbars, pagination, tooltips, shortcuts and the command palette share one item model, focus policy and event contract.
cube.actionsApi: Collection components accept items with stable id, label, description, icon, disabled, href, shortcut and selection metadata. Selection emits change; commands emit action; navigation emits navigate; popup state emits openchange. All outcome events bubble and cross shadow boundaries.
cube.actionsAccess: Native buttons and links retain keyboard behavior. Composite controls add the appropriate group, tab, menu, toolbar or navigation roles, roving focus, Home and End handling, translated names and visible focus. Supply concise labels for icon-only actions.
cube.layoutBody: Box, Row, Col, Grid and Divider provide wrapper-free layout hosts that compose through slots. They share logical sizing, spacing, surface and overflow properties and inherit all values from the active theme.
cube.layoutApi: Layout values accept normal CSS lengths or theme variables. Row supports align, justify, wrap, reverse and collapseAt. Grid supports columns, rows, autoFlow, align and justify. Divider supplies native separator semantics unless marked decorative.
cube.layoutAccess: Layout tags do not change the semantics of their slotted content. Use semantic HTML inside them. Divider exposes separator orientation, while decorative dividers are removed from the accessibility tree.
cube.overlaysBody: Modal and AlertDialog use the native dialog element for focus containment and keyboard dismissal. Flashbar provides a live notification queue. Service helpers can mount either system at the document root from any module.
cube.overlaysApi: Modal exposes show and close plus cancelable beforeopen and beforeclose events. AlertDialog adds beforeconfirm and confirm. Flashbar exposes show, updateMessage, dismiss and clear; global helpers provide the same operations without retaining an element reference.
cube.overlaysAccess: All visible and aria copy can be provided or localized. Dialogs have labelled title and description regions, Escape behavior is configurable, destructive confirmation stays explicit, and flashbar severity controls live-region urgency.
cube.mediaApi: Both players accept src, mediaTitle, muted, autoplay, loop, preload, seekStep and playbackRate. Video also accepts poster and tracks. Applications provide final translated control and status text through explicit text properties such as playLabel and errorText. All props are optional; autoplay is off by default. Methods: play, pause, stop, seek, backward, forward, setVolume, setMuted and setRate. Video supports fullscreen where the browser permits it.
cube.chartApi: CartesianChart accepts series, xAxis, yAxis, inverted, stacking and zoomable. Series types include line, spline, area, areaspline, bar, column, scatter, bubble, errorbar, x-threshold and y-threshold. Use stable series IDs. A secondary value axis is selected by its ID. Null values remain gaps; invalid values emit error rather than becoming invented data.
cube.pieApi: PieChart accepts a series containing named data segments, plus variant (pie or donut), innerTitle and innerDescription. Each segment has an id, name and value (or y). Zero-only datasets render an empty state. Negative and non-finite values are rejected gracefully. Percentages use the visible-data total.
cube.commonCharts: Both charts support heading, description, height, status and valueFormatter. Applications provide final translated status, action, table and accessibility text through explicit text properties. visibleSeries or visibleSegments makes filtering controlled; otherwise visibility is managed internally. Reassign data props after edits. select reports point selection, visibilitychange reports filters, retry requests a retry and error reports recoverable errors.
cube.accessBody: Controls use native buttons, ranges and selects with injectable translated labels. Charts provide keyboard point navigation, visible legend controls, persistent details and a data table. Reduced motion is respected. Authors must supply meaningful data names, captions and transcripts. Automated checks do not replace screen-reader and usability review.
cube.parts: Media styling parts: player, media, title, controls, play, stop, backward, forward, seek, time, volume, mute, rate, captions, fullscreen, status and transcript. Chart parts: chart, title, description, legend, legend-item, plot, graphic, navigator, details, data, table and table-cell. Use theme variables and ::part; do not target the chart engine’s private markup.
cube.audioBody: A simple audio transport with play/pause, stop, configurable seek steps, volume and playback speed. A missing source shows a safe empty state. Backward and forward seek within the current media; they are not playlist navigation.
cube.videoBody: The same transport for video, with a poster, optional caption tracks and feature-detected fullscreen. The native media node survives prop and playback updates, so controls do not restart playback.
cube.cartesianBody: A single component for common Cartesian visualizations, powered by Apache ECharts. The functional reference is Cloudscape’s Cartesian chart; this is not a React wrapper or a pixel-for-pixel copy.
cube.pieBody: One component for pie and donut views, with filtering, segment details and optional center content. ECharts is loaded only when a populated chart mounts.
cube.figma: The Studio boards in design/figma-layers are the visual source of truth; Storybook provides the runnable component reference.
cube.formNative: Select, DatePicker and TimePicker use consistent Cube rendering by default. Add the native flag only when the host browser’s native picker is preferred. Combobox provides both list and autocomplete behavior through its autocomplete property, and Calendar is available as a standalone component.
cube.popupConstraintsBody: Anchored menus and pickers size themselves to their content and stay within the viewport. Use popupMaxWidth and popupMaxHeight with a CSS length or a numeric pixel value to override the defaults; constrained content scrolls inside the popup.
cube.unitInputBody: UnitInput accepts a current unit and a units collection. A single unit is rendered as a static suffix; multiple units become a keyboard-accessible selector. Unit changes emit unitchange without changing the numeric value.
cube.selectBody: Select handles both single and multiple selection through the multi flag. Search can be enabled, disabled, or left on auto; auto displays the filter when the option count exceeds searchThreshold, which defaults to 10.
cube.formCompositionBody: Field supplies reusable label, help, details, and validation anatomy. EditableList owns accessible add, rename, reorder, and remove behavior. CodeEditor and JsonEditor provide syntax-aware editing, while LinkedValues coordinates proportional numeric fields. Applications provide all visible and accessible copy.
cube.workspaceBody: Workspace composes header, start, end, bottom, and main regions with disclosure, pointer and keyboard resizing, responsive overlays, cancelable events, and optional local persistence. It does not own application data or navigation.
cube.dataDisplayAdvancedBody: FileBrowser combines live filtering, breadcrumbs, grid and rich-table views, sorting, navigation, and controlled selection. LayerTree adds hierarchical disclosure, selection, visibility, locking, inline rename, and reordering. ExpandableSection provides the shared labelled disclosure primitive.
cube.editorPrimitivesBody: PropertyGroup composes inspector disclosure and reset behavior. SelectionOverlay, GuideOverlay, and MarqueeSelection provide controlled editor geometry and interaction without owning the application document model. Expression remains an application-level editable-field example rather than a Cube component.
cube.modalServiceBody: showModal returns a Promise-like handle with close and update methods. It accepts Nodes or content factories, async actions, custom footers, focus return, page sizing, and top- or document-layer presentation. closeAllModals invalidates outstanding workflows without requiring callers to retain component references.
cube.flashbarServiceBody: createFlashbar returns an updateable, dismissible handle. Notifications support async actions, links, error and danger aliases, controlled duration, timer pause while hovered or focused, and application-selected placement and host containers.
cube.studioCatalogBody: Importing this category or loading its browser client registers its reusable cb-* elements immediately. Components use reactive Markup templates, typed headless bases, theme variables, CSS parts, and interactive Storybook stories. Composed controls expect their required categories to be loaded by the application.
cube.studioCatalogApi: Provide visible and accessible text in the active application locale. Interactive controls emit cancelable beforechange or beforeaction events before change or action. Import a component or category to register its tags automatically. Browser scripts use the existing BFS runtime; BFS.CUBE exposes utility APIs, not component classes.
